nodes.name: Cathodic electrodeposition of Ni(OH)2
nodes.procedure: Films of Ni(OH)2 were cathodically deposited from unstirred solutions of 0.1 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (SigmaAldrich, 99.999% trace metals basis) in 18.2 MΩ·cm H2O. As-deposited Ni(OH)2 films showed no XPS signal for Fe. Typical depositions at -0.1 mA cm^{-2} for 120 s gave effective film thicknesses of ∼40 nm (see Figure S1 in the Supporting Information for a typical deposition profile and QCM frequency measurement). After deposition, films were rinsed by dipping in H2O before being transferred to the electrochemical cell.

nodes.name: Cathodic codeposition of Ni-Fe hydroxide
nodes.procedure: For films containing codeposited Fe, the total metal content in the deposition solution was held at 0.1 M, and FeCl2·4H2O (SigmaAldrich, >98%) was added. The solutions were purged with N2 gas for at least 20 min before adding FeCl2·4H2O to prevent precipitation of insoluble FeOOH. Typical depositions at -0.1 mA cm^{-2} for appropriate times gave films with controlled Fe content as determined by XPS. After deposition, films were rinsed by dipping in H2O before being transferred to the electrochemical cell. The Fe/Ni ratio in the films was higher than that in the deposition solutions.

nodes.name: Precipitation of high-purity Ni(OH)2 powder for purification
nodes.procedure: In a H2SO4-cleaned 50 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube, ∼2 g of 99.999% Ni(NO3)2·6H2O were dissolved in ∼4 mL of 18.2 MΩ·cm H2O. 20 mL of 1 M KOH were added to precipitate high-purity Ni(OH)2. The mixture was shaken and centrifuged, and the supernatant was decanted. The Ni(OH)2 then underwent three washing cycles by adding ∼20 mL of 18.2 MΩ·cm water and ∼2 mL of 1 M KOH to the tube, redispersing the solid, centrifuging, and decanting the supernatant.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Fe 2p spectra show no detectable Fe signal in as-deposited Ni(OH)_2 films and after 300 CV cycles in purified KOH, with Ni/Fe ratios of 95:5 and 98:2 after cycling in unpurified KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a shows no detectable Fe 2p XPS signal in a Ni(OH)_2 film after 300 CV cycles in the purified electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: GIXRD patterns show increased crystallinity after aging; Fe-free Ni(OH)_2 shows β-Ni(OH)_2 (001) reflection at 19° 2θ; Ni_{0.75}Fe_{0.25}(OH)_2 shows NiFe-LDH peaks at ~11° and 23.5° 2θ (003,006 reflections).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b shows GIXRD patterns for films before and after aging. All diffraction patterns show increased peak intensity after aging...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows spongy platelet-like structure; platelet size increases after aging (Fe-free: ~9±2 nm to ~12±3 nm; 25% Fe: ~20±5 nm to ~35±11 nm); films with Fe have larger platelets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows SEM images of these films before and after aging in purified 1 M KOH at 40°C for ~24 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Through-film in situ conductivity measurements show Fe-free NiOOH has σ ≈ 0.1-0.2 mS cm^{-1} while 5%-25% Fe-containing NiOOH has σ ≈ 3.5-6.5 mS cm^{-1}, a >30-fold increase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Oxidized NiOOH under Fe-free conditions has σ ≈ 0.1 to 0.2 mScm^{-1}. Samples with 5% -25% Fe have σ ≈ 3.5 to 6.5 mScm^{-1}, all more than an order of magnitude higher than that of the Fe-free films.
